en: The Great King of Teachings: The Sūtra of the Supreme Gate of Contemplation on the Secret Equality of Mañjuśrī, Scroll One.
Translated during the Song Dynasty by the State Preceptor of Qidan (Liao), from Madhyadeśa in Magadha, Central India.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Cixian. At that time, the World-Honored One was in the kingdom of Śrāvastī;
having finished his meal in the Puṣpavana Garden, he sat cross-legged.
At that moment, there were Maitreya Bodhisattva and others present.

They addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, although we have heard the profound and wondrous Dharma of the Three Vehicles, we have a slight doubt that we wish to inquire of the World-Honored One.
Beyond this Dharma-gate, are there further dharmas?"
The World-Honored One said, "Excellent, excellent!
How is it that you have been able to give rise to this question?
I possess the Mahāsamaya Secret Inner Dharma."
By practicing in reliance upon this, Mahāyāna practitioners can swiftly attain Buddhahood.
Since my attainment of Buddhahood, I have never before proclaimed it.
When Maitreya Bodhisattva and the others heard what the Buddha had said, they leaped for joy and were filled with gladness.
Having circumambulated the Buddha three times, they withdrew to stand to one side.
With their right knees touching the ground in a kneeling posture,
they joined their palms and gazed up at the World-Honored One without averting their eyes for even a moment.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Vajra-samādhi and emitted five-colored light from between his eyebrows;
within that light, he manifested the five Buddhas.
Within the blue light of the ūrṇā-kośa, he emanates Akṣobhya Buddha;
within the white light of the ūrṇā-kośa, he emanates Vairocana Buddha;
within the yellow light of the ūrṇā-kośa, he emanates Ratnasambhava Buddha.
Within the red light of the ūrṇā-kośa, he emanated Amitāyus Buddha;
within the green light of the ūrṇā-kośa, he emanated Amoghasiddhi Buddha;
and further, he emanated the Bodhisattva Vajranetra-prabhā.
The Bodhisattva Vajra-Divya-Eye Radiance,
the Bodhisattva Vajra-Dharma-Eye Radiance,
and the Bodhisattva Vajra-Jñāna-Eye Radiance.
The Bodhisattva Vajradhyāna-cakṣur-ābhāsvara (Vajra-Meditation-Eye-Light-Radiance) and these Buddhas and Bodhisattvas dwell in the first courtyard, seated in successive order.
Furthermore, they emanate eight great Bodhisattvas.
The Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhāsanetrakośa,
the Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhāsa-jihvākośa,
and the Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhāsa-ghrāṇakośa.
The Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhāsarasanidhi and the Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhākāyanidhi—
these four bodhisattvas each sit at the gates of the second court.
The Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhāsarīranidhi...
Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhāśayagarbha;
Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhājñānagarbha;
Bodhisattva Vajrajñānaprabhāprajñāgarbha.
These four bodhisattvas each sit in the four corners of the second courtyard.
Furthermore, there are twelve offering bodhisattvas,
such as the Bodhisattva Vajrapradīpaprabha.
Vajra-ghoṣa-prabha Bodhisattva,
Vajra-gandha-prabha Bodhisattva,
and Vajra-amṛta-prabha Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Vajrāmbaramatīprabha,
the Bodhisattva Vajradhvajaprabha,
and the Bodhisattva Vajranṛtyaprabha.
The Bodhisattva Vajragandhābhāsvara;
these eight bodhisattvas reside in order within the third enclosure,
seated to the left and right of the four gates.
The Bodhisattva Vajrapuṣpameghaprabha,
the Bodhisattva Vajrasūtrapuṣpaprabha,
and the Bodhisattva Vajramaṇicchatraprabha.
The Bodhisattva Vajrasādhu-prabhāsa—
these four bodhisattvas sit in order,
each occupying one of the four outer corners of the second enclosure.
Furthermore, he emanated four bodhisattvas:
the Bodhisattva Vajraprabhā-aṅkuśa and the Bodhisattva Vajraprabhā-pāśa.
The Bodhisattva Vajraprabhāśṛṅkhalā and the Bodhisattva Vajraprabhāghaṇṭā;
these four Bodhisattvas follow in this order.
Each sits at one of the four corners within the third courtyard.
From within that light, ten great vidyārājas are further emanated:
the Great Compassionate Vajra, Jvālāmukha, and Maitreyanātha.
The Vidyārāja of Great Compassion, Vajraprabha-praṇidhāna;
the Vidyārāja of Great Joy, Vajraprabha-praṇāma.
The Great Equanimity Vajra Radiance Vighnāntakṛt, the King of Illumination—
these four Kings of Illumination sit in sequence,
each occupying a position at the outer gate of the third enclosure.
The Vidyārāja Mahāprema, Vajraprabha Ṭakkirāja;
the Vidyārāja Mahācaṇḍa, Vajraprabha Nīlanetra;
and the Vidyārāja Mahābala, Vajraprabha Mahāmāla.
Vajraprabha, Ucchuṣma, Cakra, and Acala—
these four vidyārājas are seated in order at the four corners outside the third courtyard.
Below is the Vajraprabha-Vajrapāṭala Trailokyavijaya Vidyārāja;
this Vidyārāja sits facing the Vidyārāja in the eastern direction.
In the upper direction is the Vajraprabhā-uṣṇīṣa-cakravartin;
this vidyārāja sits facing the vidyārāja in the western direction.
The arrangement of these two vidyārājas is thus:
one should visualize them in the upper and lower directions.
At that time, the World-Honored One was within that light.
He manifested such miraculous transformations,
forming a great maṇḍala altar;
having manifested these, he remained.
Maitreya Bodhisattva and the others rose from their seats and,
within that assembly, questioned one another:
"Have you ever seen or heard of such inconceivable and great miraculous manifestations?"
All the great bodhisattvas, leaping for joy and shedding tears of compassion, said:
"This great supernormal transformation is profound and inconceivable;
this unprecedented dharma is wonderful and rare!"
Maitreya Bodhisattva and the others were all filled with joy and together spoke these verses:
"We leap for joy with unsurpassed delight; Now we behold the great white tuft of light in five colors.
Within this light appear many sages and worthies, Seated according to their directions, forming a maṇḍala."
Having beheld this rare and inconceivable event, I vow to practice the path equal to the All-Knowing One;
may he who expounds the gateway of compassion reveal its secret door. I prostrate and pray that he may attain unsurpassed enlightenment.
*Āhuḥ saṃghaṃ saṃghaṃ tati*. At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva, together with the great bodhisattvas and others...
Having spoken these verses together, they addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, we have already witnessed such great miraculous transformations;
out of compassion and pity for us, please explain them to us."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva and the others:
"Excellent, excellent! You all are true great beings possessed of great wisdom.
This secret dharma-gate of my samaya is difficult to believe and difficult to understand."
"What you have asked fulfills my wishes.
Upon hearing these words, Maitreya Bodhisattva and the others rose from their seats and prostrated at the four gates of the ritual arena; the assembly together recited this verse:

From beginningless time, whatever unwholesome karma we have accumulated—whether through ignorance, delusion, or under the influence of spirits—we now confess before the Bhagavān, the Greatly Compassionate One. O Tathāgata, please listen to us!
*yan nāma nidhyapayitum udyuktaḥ sarvam akuśalam karma kṣamasva saṃkalpa-pratibandhakam bhagavan mahākāruṇika mām anukampasva tathāgate śṛṇu me vācam.*
I confess my transgressions so that obstacles may be extinguished. *Mahākṛpānaprasādakara*!
To all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, to the eight classes of Nāga Kings, and to the assembly of noble ones, I bow my head and take refuge, offering homage with utmost devotion.
*Añjalīṃ kṛtvā guṇān smarāmi*. I prostrate to you all. *Namo 'stu te*.

Having recited the four aspirations and the verse beginning with "Mantravidyāvidhiṃ me nirdiśa tvaṃ tathāgata," he attained freedom from falsehood and realized bodhi; then,
having spoken thus, he addressed the Buddha.
“World-Honored One, we have been granted the sight of this maṇḍala;
what practices and vows should we undertake to cultivate this dharma-gate?
The World-Honored One replied, “First, you must receive the empowerment of the five vases.”
"I shall now expound for you the secret and essential Dharma-gate.
When the Bodhisattva Maitreya and the others heard these words,
they addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One..."
"Out of great compassion and pity,
we pray that you will accept us for initiation.
The World-Honored One replied, "You all seek to receive initiation."

For your sake, I shall empower five vases, four kinds of precious powder, water from five rivers, five kinds of incense powder, five grains, five types of seeds, five treasury items, five-colored silks, five bodhi leaves, flowers of the five seasons, five auspicious grasses, five-colored threads, five parasols, and three portions of consecrated rice.
Consecrate the five vases.
The crystal vase in the center is white,
representing the Buddha.
The vase represents the Vajra Root Pāramitā Bodhisattva.
Empower it one hundred and eight times with the Bodhisattva mantra.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ śaṅkari saṃdhikari ghuṭṭani khāṭaya sarvarakṣa saṃdhaya svāhā. With this, empower the precious vase and bestow the great empowerment.
One attains a firm body that is without birth or extinction.
The eastern agate vase,
its blue color representing the Buddha.
The vase represents the Bodhisattva Vajrapāramitā.
Empower it one hundred and eight times with the Bodhisattva mantra.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ satsva-vajri hūṃ. By this empowerment of the precious vase, one receives the great consecration and attains a vajra body, indestructible and firm.
In the south is a maṇi-jewel vase;
yellow represents the Buddha,
and the vase represents the Bodhisattva Ratnapāramitā.
Empower it one hundred and eight times with the Bodhisattva mantra.
The mantra is:
Oṃ ratnavajri tvaṃ adhiṣṭhāna-ratnaghaṭa mahābhiṣekaṃ prayaccha. (Oṃ Ratnavajri, you, empower this precious flask; bestow the great consecration.)
One obtains a body perfected with all manner of rare jewels.
To the west is a coral treasure-vase;
the red color symbolizes the Buddha.
The Bodhisattva representing the Dharma-pāramitā is the Vase.
Empower it one hundred and eight times with the Bodhisattva mantra.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ dharmavajrīcchiri. By this empowerment of the precious vase, one receives the great consecration and attains the wisdom-body of self-enjoyment.
In the north is a lapis lazuli flask;
its green color represents the Buddha,
and the flask represents the Bodhisattva of the Karma-pāramitā.
Consecrate [the vessel] one hundred and eight times with the Bodhisattva mantra.
The mantra is:
Oṃ karmavajri āḥ. Consecrate the precious vase and bestow the great empowerment.
One attains the firm bodies of the five Tathāgatas.
Regarding the mudrās of the Bodhisattvas of the five pāramitās: for the Bodhisattva Vajrapāramitā, one forms the vajra-bond with both hands.
The thumbs and index fingers are held upright like needles;
this is called the Vajra-mind Seal (Vajracitta-mudrā).
The Bodhisattva Ratnapāramitā does not alter the form of the previous seal.
Joining the *jñāna-bala* fingers with the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers,
and snapping the upper joints of the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers,
is called the Vajraratna-mudrā.
The two vajra-palms of the Bodhisattva Dharmapāramitā are like blooming lotuses,
with the fingers of the advancing and supporting hands interlocked.
Dhyāna and prajñā are also like this;
when their peaks do not touch one another,
it is called the Vajradharmamudrā.
For the Bodhisattva Karma-pāramitā, one performs the vajra-bond with both hands;
the *kṣānti*, *aṅguṣṭha*, *tarjanī*, and *madhyamā* fingers are extended upward.
This is called the Karma-mudrā.
The two hands of the Bodhisattva Vajramūlapāramitā cross at the eight fingers;
the tips of the fingers interlace within the gaps,
and the thumbs and ring fingers form the shape of a jewel.
The wisdom hand (right) presses down upon the dhyāna hand (left);
extending them, they are pressed forward with force,
while the two palms remain hollow at the heart.
This is called the Mūlā-mudrā.
With it, one consecrates the powder of the four precious substances:
gold, silver, copper, and iron.
Before these four types of precious powder have been placed into the flask,
place them together in a single vessel and [recite] the mantra of the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava and the Bodhisattva Ratnapāramitā.
Consecrate each one one hundred and eight times.
Having performed the consecration,
divide the powder of the four jewels and place it within the five vases.
Having received the great empowerment, he attained a vajra body.
He empowered the waters of the five rivers,
including the Gaṅgā River.
The Yamunā River,
the Sindhu River,
and the Vakṣu River.
The Nairañjanā River—
these five rivers represent the waters of the five Buddhas:
the Buddha-water, the Dharma-water, the Jewel-water, the Karma-water, and the Wisdom-water.
By bathing with these five waters,
all the obstructions and defilements of ordinary beings accumulated over immeasurable eons shall be purified,
and they shall attain the five auspiciousnesses.
The Buddha-śrī, Dharma-śrī, Ratna-śrī, Karma-śrī, and Jñāna-śrī—
take these five waters and place them together in a single vessel.
Then, using the mantra of the Bodhisattva Dharmapāramitā of the Buddha Amitāyus:
Each person recites [the mantra] one hundred and eight times.
Having performed the consecration,
divide the five waters and place them within five vases.
Having received the great empowerment, one attains the body of a Dharma King.
Consecrate five types of fragrant powders,
including white sandalwood incense.
Red sandalwood incense,
ox-head incense,
and kung-ku-mo incense.
Take karpūra (camphor) and these five incenses, grind them into a fine powder, and place them together in a single vessel.
Recite the mantra of the Bodhisattva Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata Karmapāramitā.
Consecrate each [incense] one hundred and eight times.
Having performed the consecration, divide the five incenses and place them within the five vases as the incenses representing the five Buddhas:
the Buddha-incense, the Dharma-incense, the Jewel-incense, the Karma-incense, and the Wisdom-incense.
By means of these five fragrances, one is conferred the Great Empowerment (mahābhiṣeka) and attains the fragrance of the Tathāgata’s fivefold Dharma-body (pañcāṅga-dharmakāya).
All undertakings and activities shall be successfully accomplished.
Consecrate the five grains:
rice, green sesame, barley, and mung beans.
Place these five grains together in a single vessel.
With the Vajra-pāramitā mantra of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya,
empower each [vessel] one hundred and eight times.
Having performed the empowerment, place them within the five vases.
Furthermore, these five grains are manifestations formed by earth, water, fire, wind, and space;
they are the seed-syllables of the five Buddhas:
the Buddha-seed, the Dharma-seed, the Jewel-seed, the Wisdom-seed, and the Vajra-seed.
The five seeds of ordinary beings circulate and transmigrate through the six realms and four modes of birth;
the five seeds of the Buddhas, having received the great consecration, abide eternally without extinction,
sustaining and empowering these five seeds.
White mustard seeds, purple mustard seeds, yellow mustard seeds, turnip seeds,
and cumin seeds— these five types of seeds should first be washed separately with pure water and then placed together in a single vessel.
Empower [the object] by reciting the mantras of the ten Great Vidyārājas seven times each.

all evil karma will naturally be extinguished,

At dusk, recite the mantra of the Eight Great Heavenly Beings for empowerment ten thousand times, as prescribed in the sutra, for either one day or one night.
Place the śarīra stūpa at the center of the maṇḍala.
Regarding the placement of the bowls,
one should observe how the presiding master of the altar (maṇḍalācārya) requests them to be set out.
After the ritual site has been dismantled, the ācārya unties the cords of the bowls.
At the time of dissolution, one should visualize extracting the disciple from the saṃsāra of the six realms.
Give the salt to the disciple to eat,
or place a small amount in water to wash the disciple’s hands and face.
When the disciple washes [the bowl],
they should imagine that they are washing away the afflictions of the six sense objects (*ṣaḍāyatana*).
Alternatively, if they do not understand this, they may set the bowl aside in a hall of merit and offer it there constantly.
At the second and fifth hours of the day, burn sandalwood incense and other offerings to the holy assembly of the altar.

In making these offerings, first offer to the Buddhas, next to the Bodhisattvas, and finally to all the devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, the four Great Heavenly Kings, and the four heavenly deities.
Constantly offer raw rice as an offering to the five ācāryas.
Visualize yourself as the Buddha of each respective direction, commanding the devas, nāgas,
and the eight classes of beings to receive the various offerings from the master of the *maṇḍala*.
Once the Ācārya and others have completed the powder mandala,
they should, at each of the four periods of the day,
visualize ascending to the upper realm to invite the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Mahādevas, and others.
Having prepared the altar with powdered [pigments], sit according to the prescribed positions.
If one lacks the capacity,
perform the offerings three times each day.
Having opened the maṇḍala until its dissolution,
if it is to be dissolved tomorrow,
then this morning at dawn, the five ācāryas [should perform the rites].
Together they sit on the western side of the maṇḍala facing east;
the Wheel-Turning King sits in the center,
and the Lotus Ācārya sits to the south.
The Ratna-ācārya sits next to the south;
the Vajra-ācārya sits to the north of the Wheel-turning King (Cakravartin);
and the Karma-ācārya sits next to the north.
Each of the five ācāryas shall recite the mantra of the Buddha of their respective direction ten thousand times and the mantra of the Bodhisattva one thousand times.
While reciting the mantras aloud, they should focus their minds exclusively on visualizing the radiant and brilliant splendor of the bodies of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Once the recitation and chanting were completed,
the ācāryas each sat according to their respective directions;
having rung their bells, performed the recitations, and presented various offerings, they concluded.
Nevertheless, each person enters into contemplation,
visualizing themselves performing repentance, exhorting, rejoicing, dedicating merit, and making vows together with the presiding master of the ritual site;
meanwhile, the ācāryas and others remain within the state of contemplation.
Either the body experiences a shivering sensation or perspiration breaks out;
or one sees auspicious signs in dreams;
or auspicious matters are praised from within the sky.
Alternatively, if the master of the ritual site has personal matters of great auspiciousness,
one may likewise emerge from contemplation as before,
perform repentance and make vows together with the master of the ritual site, and so forth.
Furthermore, for any matters where offerings were not fully completed or where recitations were erroneous,
each person shall perform repentance before the altar on behalf of the master of the ritual site and pray for auspiciousness.
At the fifth watch of the night, the ācāryas and the master of the practice hall [shall proceed].
Having each bathed and rinsed their mouths,
they were provided with the preparations for the empowerment by the master of the maṇḍala;
meanwhile, the master had them stand in a separate, purified chamber.
Master Ximen commanded the presiding master of the maṇḍala to give rise to the bodhicitta,
practice loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, and receive the samaya-dharma.
He then gave various instructions and questioned the presiding master of the maṇḍala, saying:

"Can you uphold all that has been explained above? He asked this three times, and the disciple answered "Yes" three times. Then, Ācārya Ratnasaṃbhava tied a silk cloth around the waist of his disciple.

Leading the disciple to the eastern gate, he performed prostrations; having next paid homage at the southern, western, and northern gates, he then prostrated at the center of the eastern gate and offered incense.
Instruct the disciple to open their vajra-palms in the gesture of holding an object.
While holding the flower within their palms, have them cast it onto the maṇḍala;
identify the deity according to where the flower lands.
Having acknowledged this,
the Vajrācārya instructs the disciple:
"Do not be conceited in mind, and do not speak of this to those who have not entered the maṇḍala."
The speaker incurs the offense of a vajra-sin.
Once the Vajrācārya has untied the silk cloth,
the Ratnācārya leads the disciple to the southern gate.
Instruct [the disciple] to kneel with the right knee on the ground,
join the palms, and face the mandala;
the ācārya stands with his back to the mandala.
The ācārya visualizes himself as the deity Ratnasaṃbhava and performs the bodhisattva-vase consecration,
or the conch-water consecration.
The *karmācārya* leads the disciple around the maṇḍala seven times and performs prostrations at the five gates.
They offer incense, food, drink, and various other offerings;
furthermore, they present various gifts and benefits to the holy assembly within the maṇḍala precincts and to the various devas.
The five ācāryas shall bestow material gifts according to their respective means, without calculating the value or profit.
The karma-ācārya shall cause the disciple to stand at the northern gate, facing the maṇḍala.
With the right knee touching the ground in the kneeling posture (hukuei) and palms joined,
the ācārya stands with his back to the altar.
He points the ritual scepter (kīla) at the crown of the disciple’s head as prescribed in the sūtra.
Having visualized the syllables of the various Buddhas, noble ones,
and the knowledge of all modes (*sarvajñajñāna*), finally point to the disciple’s heart and personally recite the mantra of the *iṣṭadevatā* three times.
Place the vajra horizontally across the disciple’s joined palms;
the disciple holds it with the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers,
while the *ācārya* holds it with the *kṣānti* finger.
The master places his palms together with those of the disciple;
the remaining four fingers grasp the eight peaks of the disciple’s joined palms.

Shaking the bell with the left hand, he recites the praises of the five Buddhas as explained in the sūtra. The ācārya himself offers one portion of the consecrated rice (*pūjā-bali*) from the garland of flowers.
Place them before the disciple.
Having arranged various offerings such as incense, flowers, lamps, and ointments,
the ācārya himself places the crown upon [the disciple].
Having arranged the aforementioned articles and other offerings for the disciple,
the master personally holds a mirror before the disciple’s face and causes the disciple to gaze into it.
The Ācārya Padma said:
"When a disciple sees their own reflection in a mirror,
they must contemplate it as being their own body."
At the time of the consecration, although one possesses an impermanent body,
one should conceive of it as having attained an eternal body, identical to the body of a Buddha.
Having spoken thus, the disciple immediately rises.
The Ācārya Padma had his disciple recite the mantra of the tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā) that he had identified,
either by constant recitation or for a period of six months.
Alternatively, if the disciple seeks the teachings extensively, the master may grant them as they wish.
When the meal of the fast-day is finished,
the Ācārya Padma explains to the disciple the teachings previously bestowed.
When evening arrived, the five ācāryas together prepared ten portions of raw rice.

Each performed the empowerment and offering at their respective gates; having thus empowered and offered to the Wheel-Turning King (Cakravartin) and to the upper and lower directions, the ācārya performed the empowerment and offering.
The master of the site of enlightenment arranged five young boys and five young girls,
five golden saddles and bridles for horses, and five milch cows,
all of which were offered to the holy assembly at the five gates.
For each gate, he bestowed four mu of tax-exempt land along with its crops—namely rice, large and small wheat, and so forth;
no other crops were permitted.
He also provided five beds, five mattresses, and five pairs of new garments.
Five pairs of shoes, five sets of *homakunda* implements,
five pairs of bells and vajras, brocade and silk, various sutras, gold, silver, and the seven precious gems—
all these are to be offered before the five *ācāryas*.
The ācāryas and others each sit with their backs to the mandala.
Each visualizes his own body as the fundamental deity of the respective gate,
receiving the offerings and benefits from the disciples.
The ritual implements and other articles are each placed at the feet of the ācārya.
The disciple burns incense and first pays homage to the ācārya at the eastern gate.
Having finished the prostration, [he proceeds].
The Master takes the disciple’s right hand with his own right hand and leads him to the presence of the Ācārya at the southern gate; having performed the prostrations,
they stand before him.
The Master of the Eastern Gate leads [the assembly] back,
and they sit according to their original positions;
all subsequent instances follow this precedent.
Having been led to the northern gate and performed the rites,
the ācārya of the northern gate takes the disciple’s right hand with his own right hand and proceeds to the eastern gate to pay respects to the ācārya of the center.
He has the disciple sit at the eastern gate with his right knee on the ground and palms joined.
The five ācāryas stand together at the eastern gate, each positioned according to their respective direction and holding the flask assigned to that direction.
The disciple stands in the center.
Each of the five ācāryas visualizes themselves situated in their respective directions.
Having recited the mantra for escorting the noble assembly three times as prescribed in the sūtra, the karma-ācārya says:
The disciple must imagine himself seated at the center of the maṇḍala.
He should visualize the maṇḍala as a palace or pavilion.
The five ācāryas should likewise imagine themselves escorting the assembly of noble beings.
While remaining in space, upon the sound of a single clap of hands, [the deities] arrived and took their places.
The five masters each held a directional flask and simultaneously poured water over the disciple’s head;
the master in the center poured from his flask over the disciple’s head.
The preceptor causes the disciple to drink it.
The *karmācārya* says: "The five masters confer the empowerment upon the disciple’s crown.
The disciple visualizes that he is being consecrated by the five Buddhas.
When the five masters perform the consecration,
each visualizes themselves as one of the five Buddhas in the space before them as previously described;
having thus consecrated the crown of the disciple’s head, they proceed.
He instructs the disciples to rise and prostrate at the altar site from the eastern gate.
After each prostration,
the respective gate *ācāryas* take a pinch of colored powder from atop the altar.
He rubbed the heads of his disciples with his hand.
Then, he took a small portion for himself and his disciples to eat.
Following the instructions of the Master, the disciples each visualized their own bodies as the body of a Buddha of that particular direction.
He proceeded to the north gate and prostrated;
having arrived at the east gate and prostrated once more, the central ritual was completed.
Thereupon, he paid his respects to the five ācāryas.
Afterwards, the five masters gather together at the mandala; within the center, beneath a white parasol, they visualize it as the form of a stūpa.
While gathering the colored powders:
Each of the five masters should imagine [the stupa] as being like a Buddha-stūpa.
Once they have gathered together, the five masters should each, according to their respective positions and portions, offer incense and flowers;
thereafter, they may walk about at will.
On the following day, place colored powders within a clean vessel,
tie them into a decorative canopy, and set it inside. Then,
have a *śūdra* (lay attendant) bathe, don new clothes, and carry it forth.
A grand procession was formed, led by banners of majestic deportment, pennants, conchs, cymbals, and musical instruments.
Following behind were the five ācāryas and the master of the maṇḍala,
who together escorted the powdered remains of the altar into the sandbars of the river.
Construct a stūpa shape with four gates; at each gate,
visualize the Buddha of that respective direction, and at the central gate,
visualize the form of the Buddha who has attained enlightenment.
Each of the five masters extensively performed various ritual services and offerings at their respective gates,
reciting the liturgical prayers three times throughout the day and night for a full twenty-four hours.
Then, having performed the homa fire offering and worship,
the five masters shall make vows and repent on behalf of the disciples and their retinues, dedicating the merit thereof.
May it universally moisten all sentient beings so that they may together attain the Buddha-way.
Having performed this dedication,
the disciple escorted the five ācāryas back to their vihāra.
After three days had passed, the five masters again instructed their disciples to prepare offerings according to their means at the site of the maṇḍala,
constructing a small altar using the dung of a milch cow.
Place a *caoro* (flat gong) on top and a *śarīra* stupa inside it.
Elevate the stupa using a clean object.
Next, place river water inside the *caoro*.
When entering the water, each of the five masters should visualize bathing the five Buddhas.
Then, in each of the four directions, arrange one portion of cooked rice and one portion of raw rice for each Buddha.
In the eastern direction, place two lamps, each one vessel, and a single incense burner.
Each of the five ācāryas casts one hundred and eight lotus flowers into the cymbal-bowl one hundred and eight times.
Then, the Wheel-Turning King ācārya offers the iron spoon into the milk-rice.
When it is time for the recitation of the full number of mantras,
one should likewise place [the vessel] in water and visualize it being placed within the Buddha’s mouth.
After the five masters have each rung their bells and performed various ritual services and offerings, [the procedure is complete].
Discard the raw rice in a clean place; give the Buddha’s rice to the poor.
All offerings contained within the cauldron and other vessels shall be sent to the river on the following morning.
On the seventh day, the five masters again prepared offerings according to their means.
Having performed the consecration and the sacrifice to the local deities (jishen),
the five masters themselves removed the altar mud and animal skins and cast them into the river.
As for the earth from the altar,
the presiding master of the Way’s altar shall have a *śuddhakarmakara* (pure attendant) carry it to a clean location.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha, having finished expounding this secret dharma of the ritual arena (*maṇḍala*), [spoke further].
He addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: "If there are kings,
ministers, elders, householders, brahmins, and others, as well as the fourfold assembly,
who establish this maṇḍala according to the Dharma and receive the great empowerment to practice such rites as these."
These are truly the sons of the Dharma King.
All the five crimes of immediate retribution, the ten unwholesome karmas,
and all other grave offenses committed by these people throughout past kalpas shall be completely extinguished.
Even if the nation faces calamities, they shall naturally be extinguished.
It is like a single spark of fire that can consume ten thousand bundles of stacked firewood;
one will attain the fulfillment of the ten pāramitās with absolute certainty and without doubt.
The benefits obtained are difficult to describe in full.
These Dharma princes and others are all praised together by the Buddhas and Tathāgatas;
this person will certainly attain perfect enlightenment before long.
After the end of their lives, they will be reborn in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
There, they shall behold Amitāyus Buddha,
hear the Dharma of non-retrogression, and become equal to the Buddhas.
Furthermore, if there is a person who, following the instructions of their teacher, sprinkles water empowered within the ritual mandala upon themselves and others,
and practices this rite accordingly, after the end of their life—
One may take birth at will in the pure lands of the ten directions. Furthermore, if there is a person who constructs this Mañjuśrī maṇḍala and receives the empowerment,
instructions, and blessings according to the master’s teachings,
as soon as they perform this rite, in this very life—
The eight classes of devas and nāgas constantly come to protect them, all of whom revere and honor them.
The Four Great Heavenly Kings also come to protect them as they would protect the Buddhas.
Wherever these practitioners travel, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, along with their retinues, ministers, and followers, shall likewise provide protection.
They spread out celestial robes for him to tread upon and constantly served as attendants to those travelers.
These travelers had not yet given rise to the mind of great compassion nor made the vow to attain Buddhahood.
Furthermore, I pray that in a future age I may become a Great Wheel-Turning King to protect the Buddha-dharma,
constantly practicing the ten wholesome paths to benefit sentient beings,
and fulfill my vow to take the form of various kings, both great and small.
Constantly transforming others through the True Dharma,
I also vow to become a great Dharma Master to open the eyes and ears of sentient beings,
turning the Great Wheel of Dharma to bring benefit to all living beings.
All that they wish for and delight in shall be completely fulfilled.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi:
"I declare that this Dharma was not proclaimed by me."
This has been proclaimed in common by all the Buddhas of the past; do not give rise to doubt or difficulty.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who seeks such a Dharma and wishes to hear, receive, and uphold it, they should first establish the Mañjuśrī maṇḍala.
Before each of the Buddhas and the assembly of holy beings at the ritual site,
one should generate a heart of profound reverence and prepare various offerings.
Having received the great empowerment, one may then listen to, receive, and uphold [the teachings].
Whatever beneficial deeds have been performed, even in their most minimal portions,
I dedicate them all to sentient beings, vowing that they may achieve the unsurpassed fruit. Furthermore,
if there are those who do not rely on the instructions of a master, do not establish this maṇḍala, and do not receive the great empowerment;
One must never allow them to see or hear it, nor permit them to enter the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, if anyone should secretly listen to this Dharma, they will incur immeasurable sin.
Moreover, if there is someone who has received this Dharma...
With both hands, he should cup the right foot of the preceptor and place it upon his own crown.
The preceptor says: "From this day forward, you must regard all sentient beings and constantly give rise to great compassion."
The elder should regard them as parents, and those younger than oneself as siblings;
with all available offerings of incense, flowers, lamps, and ointments,
one should mentally present these to the assembly of noble beings within the ritual mandala.
And making offerings to all sentient beings,
one should not differ from making offerings to the Buddha;
they are entirely equal, even including those of different species.
First, visualize the Buddhas within various types of bodies;
above a white parasol, there is a jeweled pavilion,
and one should also visualize bathing the Buddhas.
Having bathed the Buddha with the water of ambrosia, one now bathes it again for the sake of other beings.
By virtue of these merits,
may all be liberated from saṃsāra and obtain the seeds of Buddhahood.
If there are those who harbor doubt or arrogance regarding this Dharma,
do not proclaim it to them.
If there are those who do not begrudge their own bodies or lives for the sake of this Dharma, [then you may teach it].
Even unto those who seek this Dharma with a sincere and earnest mind, the Precept-Transmitting Ācārya must not harbor a mind of stinginess regarding the Dharma.

At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken this Dharma, the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati rose from his seat, circumambulated the Buddha three times, withdrew to stand to one side, and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
Although we have already seen and heard [of this],
we have never before encountered such a secret method of practice involving the visualization of a great powder mandala;
we shall now practice solely according to this dharma-gate.
Furthermore, by relying on what dharma does one practice it?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, saying:
"I have realized bodhi."
Furthermore, you should receive and uphold the mantras of the noble assembly of the Great Maṇḍala altar, which were collectively proclaimed by all the Buddhas of the past.
By receiving and upholding them, you shall swiftly attain Buddhahood.
"Listen attentively, and I shall speak for you.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, out of great compassion, please expound this for us; we wish to hear it.
At that time, the World-Honored One immediately spoke the mantra for the inexhaustible merit of requesting [the Dharma], saying:

*Namo buddhāya* | *Namo dharmāya* | *Namo saṃghāya* | *Namo śrīmanmune* | *Tathāgatāya* | *Rahate* | *Samyaksaṃbuddhāya* | *Oṃ amṛtabhava* | *Vipulagarbha* | *Pravarabodhisattva* | *Siddhyasva mahāgarbhe* | *Dhana dhana svāhā*. At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this mantra, [remained silent].
He addressed the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, saying:
"If there is a practitioner of the Mahāyāna who establishes this maṇḍala and invites the five ācāryas..."
At each respective gate,
one should offer pure water, sprinkle scented water, apply fragrant ointments, scatter seasonal flowers, burn lamps of ghee,
and present all various offerings, dedicating them all completely.
Recite these secret mantras seven times for each.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, saying:
"You should receive and uphold the mantras of the holy assembly of the Great Maṇḍala altar of Universal Invitation."
If you uphold this, you will be able to escape the evil realms and rescue all sentient beings.
If there is a practitioner who establishes this maṇḍala, they should invite five ācāryas and recite this mantra according to the gates; whenever any offerings are presented, [they should do so].
Constantly recollecting all the Buddhas, one should chant this secret mantra.
The Universal Invitation Mantra is as follows: Namo ratnatrayāya | namo 'rhatām.
Śrī-kṛtaye mātḥ-sattvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā oṃ akṣaraya vimale.

*Pulakalavi svāhā.* At that time, having spoken this mantra,
the World-Honored One again addressed the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati.
You should receive and uphold the mantra for purifying internal and external bonds.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who establishes a ritual mandala and invites five ācāryas, they should silently recite this mantra at each gate to empower pure water.
Using this pure water with one's own palms,
by sprinkling it upon one’s own crown and drinking it,
one will be able to eliminate calamities and adversities and attain great auspiciousness.
Furthermore, when sprinkling water upon the paths of the maṇḍala as the presiding master of the site,
or when sprinkling all the articles of offering and so forth,
one should silently recite this mantra to empower them.
Then he spoke the mantra for purifying internal and external fetters, saying:
Oṃ vigatavaraṇa-samantapariśodhani oṃ maṇi maṇi khara khara kṣaya-arghade hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. Bodhisattva Akṣayamati.
Furthermore, there are mantras for universally invoking the Tathāgatas Amitābha, Akṣobhya, and Vairocana;
one should also receive and uphold the seed-syllables of the three Buddhas' wisdom-knowledge.
Furthermore, if there is a person who establishes a ritual mandala and invites five ācāryas,
each should visualize themselves as the precious pavilion of Śākyamuni Buddha.
Nevertheless, one should invite the three Buddhas and visualize the Knowledge of All Modes (*sarvajñatā*).
Recite this mantra of universal invitation seven times:
Oṃ mīri mīri mīri mīri gale gale kṣare kṣare anta haṃ chuḥ anta-ya-lu muṇi muṇi prasara prasara kṣaye svāhā. The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati:

Furthermore, there are the mantras for universally invoking the eight great bodhisattvas, the four great devas, the four great heavenly kings, and the four great heavenly goddesses; you should receive and uphold them.
If there are sentient beings who constantly make offerings and silently recite and maintain them, [they shall obtain great benefits].
One can utterly eliminate obstacles and afflictions and attain great wisdom;
one can open the five eyes and benefit immeasurable beings.
Then, he spoke the mantra for Universal Entreaty:

*Namo ratnatrayāya | Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya | Bodhisattvāya | Mahāsattvāya | Mahākāruṇikāya | Ehyehi | Prasannakuṭu | Tadyathā | Kuḷe kuḷe | Kuḷe vīrya | Svāhā.* Furthermore, Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, there is another mantra for the universal offering to the eight great bodhisattvas.
I shall now proclaim it:
if there are sentient beings who reverently make offerings to and silently recite and uphold this,
they will enable those beings to attain the four kinds of unimpeded eloquence and increase their merit and virtue.
Then he spoke the mantra for Universal Offering, which says:
NAMAḤ SIDDHYOGANĀTAPARŪKṢAHITAKAMPAYA NAMAḤ SIDDHIVAIŚVARŪPAYA SARVAVĀGVIJÑĀNĀYA NAMO NAMAḤ. Next, the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati.
I have this mantra for taking refuge in and making offerings to the Great Vajra King Deity; you should receive and uphold it.
If there are sentient beings who silently recite and maintain it while making offerings of incense and flowers, [they shall attain success].
It is capable of uprooting sentient beings from the three realms and enabling them to attain great bodhi.
He then spoke the mantra for taking refuge and making offerings, as previously described.
Furthermore, the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati has another mantra for taking refuge and making offerings to the Great Great Deity; you should receive and uphold it.
If there are sentient beings who silently recite and uphold [this] while making various kinds of offerings,
they will be attended by all the Buddhas, devas, and nāgas;
their merit is immeasurable and difficult to fully proclaim.
Then he spoke the mantra for taking refuge and making offerings, saying:

*Oṃ namas sarvāya santāya karanatraya hetave jinejyāmi jadamānām tvaṅgate pramiśvarā āti svāhā*. Furthermore, Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, you should receive and uphold this mantra for taking refuge and making offerings to Maheśvara: [mantra follows].
If there are sentient beings who respectfully make offerings to and silently recite and uphold [this],
they shall enable those beings to escape saṃsāra and attain great mastery.
[The deity] will personally protect them and cause the seekers' wishes to be fulfilled.
Then he spoke the mantra for taking refuge and making offerings:

Oṃ namo mahānīlavāya, mahākapilavāya, mahāmahiṣarāya, sarvanivartapūjita, namas-kṛtāya svāhā. Furthermore, Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, you should receive and uphold this mantra for taking refuge and making offerings to the Great Black Deity: [Mantra follows].
If there are sentient beings who constantly make offerings to and silently recite this dhāraṇī,
all their undertakings shall be brought to fulfillment.
Then he spoke the mantra for taking refuge and making offerings:

Oṃ namo mahākālāya tṛpragaranāhanāya sarvanīvāpabhañjanāya sarvabhayaviyogatrāṇakāraya svāhā. Furthermore, Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, there is another mantra for universally summoning the Four Great Heavenly Kings which you should receive and uphold.
If there are sentient beings who constantly make offerings to and silently recite and uphold [this],
they will be able to eliminate obstacles and afflictions and attain great auspiciousness;
they will possess wealth, nobility, and sovereignty, and their lifespan will be extended.
Then he spoke the mantra for the universal exhortation (*sarvaprārthanā*):
Oṃ namo caṇḍamahāroṣaṇāya vīraṇakāya vīraprakṣāya dṛḍha-taḥ.
raḥ ṣṭhaṃ kuvera-naiti śraṃ sarva-nivānāṃ pūjyānandīpunaḥ punaḥ sarva-malānāṃ sarva-dvāpa sarva.
Nir-ṭi-va-tsa-phala-va-sa-tra-ca-tsa-tsi-tsa-ma-na-ni-pra-ṇi-pa-ti-ye-ja-ga-ta-yu-ru-oṃ śrī.
Vaimacchara-mānaya puruṣam agne namaḥ svāhā.
Furthermore, Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, there are the mantras for the Goddess of Universal Invitation,
the Goddess of Precious Speech, the Goddess of Auspiciousness, and the Goddess who Subdues Māra.
You should receive and uphold this.
If there are sentient beings who, according to their capacity, make offerings and silently recite and maintain it,
the four great goddesses will constantly bring great benefit to those sentient beings.
In all matters, whether preparing ritual altars or undertaking various activities,
may you grant your protection so that everything may be brought to perfect completion.
Then, he spoke the mantra for universally summoning the four great goddesses:
Oṃ akṣamāṇi māyena hūṃ arjakyuvīya seṣubhābhyanāya nāmuñcuśriyāya kuḥ.
Mārabuddhaya tanyatā oṃ śrīgarbhe maṇigarbhe piyanagarbhā mā samantagarbha.
*Ṛṣibhūrja-vajriṇi svāhā*.
Furthermore, Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, there is a mantra of the Dharma-speaking goddess; you should receive and uphold it.
If there are sentient beings who constantly recite and uphold [this] in silence, or who constantly make offerings,
these individuals will in this present life attain great wisdom and clear memory such that they never forget.
Thereupon, he spoke the mantra of the Dharma-speech goddess:

Oṃ namo sarasvatyai namaḥ saptavidyācakravartini vinīraṇi kṛśami siddhibhavatu me svāhā. Furthermore, Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, you should receive and uphold this mantra of the goddess Ratnādhipatidevī.
If there are sentient beings who constantly recite it silently, uphold it, and offer worship and respect,
such persons will, in this present life, have little illness and little affliction;
no non-human spirits shall find an opportunity to harm them, and they shall be free from all calamities and disasters.
Then he spoke the mantra of the goddess Ratnaprabhā, the Mistress of Jewels, as follows:

*Namo sṭuhariteye | naśanīgarukapālaśce | sarvavidāraṇa-krīḍe kuru mantu | sarvavikriyāṃ haraṇi | hariteye svāhā.* Furthermore, Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, there is also the mantra of the goddess Śrī; you should receive and uphold it.
If there are sentient beings who make offerings, pay respect, and silently recite and uphold [this],
such persons will enjoy wealth, nobility, and mastery in their present life,
and in future lives they shall obtain a perfect physical form.
Then he spoke the mantra of the goddess Śrī:

Oṃ śrī-vare oṃ śrī-lakṣmi oṃ śrī-yaśasvini oṃ śrī-maheśvari maheśvara-namadraṇi śrī-nivayasaśvini svāhā. Furthermore, Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, there is the mantra of the goddess Māra-damini; you should receive and uphold it.
If there are sentient beings who make offerings, pay respect, and silently recite and uphold [this],
all the mundane undertakings they engage in shall be accomplished in this very life,
and no celestial Māras shall be able to find an opportunity to harm them.
He then spoke the mantra for subduing the celestial maidens (*devakanyā*), saying:

Oṃ vajrakurukulle svāhā | Mahācaṇḍe mahāvijaye svāhā | Mahāmāheśvarī mahāsaṅkari mahāsaṅkari mahānaṭini viśvaviśve svāhā | Māheśvari sarvārthasiddhikari namaḥ svāhā | Furthermore, Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, there is a mantra for blessing food and drink which you should receive and uphold: [Mantra follows] ...svāhā |
If in a future age there should be a Dharma-preacher who takes small portions of various foods and places them together in a single vessel,
sitting before the altar with them resting in his left palm;
Recite this mantra seven times with focused mindfulness.
At each dusk, go outside the mandala and scatter [the offerings] toward the ten directions with your right hand.
Those who are unable to enter the great maṇḍala will be honored by devas and spirits;
by relying on this method, their aspirations shall be fulfilled.
It is also called the "Mantra for Seeking Truth.
Then he spoke the mantra for blessing food and drink, saying:

*Namo ratnatrayāya | namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya | bhaṭṭārakāya | mahāsattvāya | mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | kule kule | kule viye | svāhā.* Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, there is furthermore a mantra that wards off all evil māras and eliminates calamities and misfortunes; you should receive and uphold it.
If in a future age there should be a missionary who takes a single thread and mixes it with fresh butter and yellow mustard seeds,
he should empower it by reciting this mantra twenty-one times.
If this thread is used to demarcate the boundaries of a ritual site (*maṇḍala*),
no evil māras will be able to enter.
If there is a sick person, one should tie this thread around their neck.
When binding [the thread], empower it twenty-one times with this mantra; the illness will then be cured.
Burn fresh butter and yellow mustard seeds in a fire;
by fumigating the master of the ritual site (*maṇḍala*), their grave sins will be extinguished.
If there is a sick person, one should burn this fresh butter (*navanīta*) together with yellow mustard seeds and fumigate the patient’s nose and their bedding; the illness will be cured immediately.
While performing the fumigation, one should also recite this mantra twenty-one times to empower it.
Alternatively, one may empower pure water to demarcate the boundaries of the ritual arena;
by reciting this mantra, malevolent spirits will be unable to enter.
If there is a sick person, one should empower pure water for them.
Recite this mantra twenty-one times;
by sprinkling consecrated water upon the patient, the illness will be immediately cured.
If there are sentient beings who constantly recite and uphold it, [the same shall occur].
All calamities and afflictions shall be extinguished.
Then he spoke this mantra for the elimination of disasters and the removal of misfortunes:
*Oṃ tadyathā ciri ciri mame ciri tuṇa tuṇa mahātuṇa jvala jvala mahājvala hili hili mahāhili svāhā*. At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this Mahāsamaya Secret Dharma...
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, Maitreya Bodhisattva and the others leaped for joy and,
with faith and reverence, accepted and practiced it.
*The Great King of Teachings Sūtra on the Supreme Gate of Contemplation of the Secret Equality of Mañjuśrī*, Fascicle Five.
